info.name: Compliance Buddy v3
info.description:
# Compliance Buddy v3 — Full API Collection

Autonomous AI-powered security remediation platform.

## Setup
1. Import this collection into Postman
2. Import `CB_v3_local.postman_environment.json` as an environment
3. Select the **CB Local (k3d)** environment
4. Ensure `compliance-buddy.local` resolves (`127.0.0.1 compliance-buddy.local` in hosts file)
5. Start the cluster: run `start-cb.ps1`

## Auth
All requests use **X-API-Key** header (set at collection level). Default value: `dev-key-change-in-prod`.

## Internal Services (port-forward required)
Services other than cb-api are not exposed via Ingress. Use kubectl port-forward to access their health/actuator endpoints:
```
kubectl port-forward svc/<service> <local>:<remote> -n cb-system
```

## Swagger UI
http://compliance-buddy.local/swagger-ui/index.html

## Grafana / Prometheus
- Grafana: http://localhost:3000 (admin/admin)
- Prometheus: http://localhost:9090

item.name: 🔍 Scanner — Trigger Scans
item.description: Trigger on-demand SonarQube scans (cb-scanner). Publishes VulnerabilityKafkaEvent to vulnerabilities.detected topic.

request.description:
Triggers an immediate SonarQube poll for the given project key (instead of waiting for the 5-minute scheduled poll).

**No request body required.** The `{projectKey}` path variable must match a key in SCANNER_PROJECTS env var on cb-scanner.

**Response:**
```json
{ "newFindings": 3, "status": "SCAN_COMPLETE", "projectKey": "my-app" }
```
Triggers scan on the `payment-service` SonarQube project. Change the path to any project key.

request.description: Returns only CRITICAL severity vulnerabilities (routed to GPT-4o for fix generation).

All vulnerabilities for a specific project.

request.description: MAJOR severity vulnerabilities — routed to qwen2:7b (Ollama) in v3.

Returns full detail for one vulnerability. **Set `vuln_id`** collection variable first (auto-saved by 'List All Vulnerabilities' test script).

**Response fields:** id, projectKey, ruleKey, cweId, severity, status, component, line, message, createdAt, updatedAt

exec: console.log('Vuln status:', v.status, '| Severity:', v.severity, '| CWE:', v.cweId);

request.description:
Re-queues a vulnerability for AI fix generation by publishing a new `VulnerabilityKafkaEvent` to the `vulnerabilities.detected` topic. Useful for vulnerabilities stuck in FAILED state or after model changes.

**No request body required.**

**Response:** `{ "queued": true, "vulnerabilityId": "..." }`

item.name: 🔧 Fixes
item.description: AI-generated fix records including unified diff patches, model used, confidence scores, and build logs.

request.description:
Returns all AI-generated fix records. Each fix contains the unified diff patch, the model used, confidence score, token count, and build log.

**Response fields per item:** id, vulnerabilityId, diff (unified patch text), model, confidence (0.0–1.0), tokensUsed, cacheHit, status, buildLog, branch, patchedBranch, createdAt

Returns a single fix including the full unified diff patch.

**Set `fix_id`** variable first (auto-saved by 'List All Fixes' test script).

**Key fields to inspect:**
- `diff` — the unified patch applied to the source file
- `confidence` — LLM confidence score (0–1). Values < 0.70 are blocked by OPA.
- `model` — which LLM generated this fix
- `cacheHit` — true if served from Redis prompt cache
- `buildLog` — stdout from `./gradlew build test`

exec: console.log('Model:', f.model, '| Confidence:', f.confidence, '| Cache hit:', f.cacheHit);

item.name: 📊 Metrics & Dashboard
item.description: Pipeline KPIs: vulnerability counts by status, fix counts by model, remediation rate.

item.name: 💰 Cost Tracking
item.description: LLM API spend tracking. Breaks down cost by model and by CWE type. Useful for verifying Ollama local inference is reducing GPT-4o spend.

request.description: Monthly LLM cost breakdown across all models.

Shows which CWE types cost the most to remediate — useful for identifying CWEs where fine-tuned local models would save the most money.

**Response:** `[{ cweId, totalCostUsd, totalTokens, fixCount }]` sorted by cost desc

exec: console.log('Most expensive CWE:', data[0].cweId, '| Cost: $', data[0].totalCostUsd);

request.description:
Shows spend per LLM model. Use this to confirm Ollama local models are actually being used for MAJOR/MINOR/INFO vulnerabilities (cost = $0.00).

**Response:** `[{ model, totalCostUsd, totalInputTokens, totalOutputTokens, fixCount }]`

item.name: 📋 Audit Trail
item.description: Full audit trail of all pipeline actions: status transitions, OPA decisions, PR creation, escalations.

request.description:
Returns all audit events across all modules. Includes vulnerability status transitions, fix generation, PR creation, OPA decisions, and escalations.

**Response fields per event:** id, entityId, entityType, action, actor, details (JSON), timestamp

Returns all audit events for a specific entity (vulnerability ID, fix ID, etc.).

**Set `entity_id`** variable to any vulnerability or fix ID. Auto-saved by 'List All Fixes' test script.

Useful for tracing the full lifecycle of one vulnerability from DETECTED → RESOLVED.

item.name: ⚙️ Actuator & Monitoring
item.description: Spring Boot Actuator endpoints: Prometheus metrics scrape, application info, beans, environment.

request.description:
Returns all Prometheus metrics in text/plain format. Prometheus scrapes this endpoint every 15 seconds.

**Key CB metrics to look for:**
- `cb_vulnerabilities_detected_total`
- `cb_fixes_generated_total`
- `cb_prs_created_total`
- `cb_escalations_triggered_total`
- `cb_llm_cost_usd_total`
- `cb_llm_tokens_total`
- `cb_fix_confidence`
- `cb_pipeline_duration_seconds`
- `cb_redis_cache_hit_total`

Returns active Spring profiles and environment properties (sanitized — credentials are masked as *****).

**Note:** Only accessible if `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=env` is set in application.yml.
Lists all Spring beans loaded in the application context. Useful for verifying Kafka listeners, ChatClient beans, and LangGraph4j workflow beans are registered.

item.name: 🤖 MCP Server (AI Tools)
item.description: Model Context Protocol SSE endpoint for AI assistants. Connect Claude Desktop or Cursor to interact with 12 CB tools via natural language.

request.description:
Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoint for the Model Context Protocol server.

**Used by:** Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible AI assistants.

**Not a REST API** — this is a streaming SSE connection. Opening this in Postman shows the raw SSE stream. Use Claude Desktop or Cursor to invoke the 12 MCP tools.

**12 Available MCP Tools:**
1. `findPreviousFixes` — search past fixes by CWE
2. `getSonarIssue` — fetch SonarQube issue detail
3. `getPRDiff` — get GitHub PR diff
4. `buildProject` — trigger Gradle/Maven build
5. `createPR` — create a GitHub PR
6. `getBuildLog` — fetch build log for a fix
7. `searchPastIncidents` — semantic search over escalations
8. `queryQdrant` — direct Qdrant vector search
9. `regenerateFix` — force re-run LangGraph4j for a vulnerability
10. `getTrace` — fetch Tempo trace by traceId
11. `getMetrics` — fetch Prometheus metric values
12. `triggerRollback` — rollback a merged CB PR

**Port-forward:**
```
kubectl port-forward svc/cb-mcp-server 8086:8086 -n cb-system
```
Then set Claude Desktop MCP config to: `http://localhost:8086/sse`
Health check for cb-mcp-server (requires port-forward to :8086).

item.name: 🧪 End-to-End Workflow
item.description: Run these 6 steps in sequence to test the full pipeline: Trigger scan → detect vulns → AI fix → build validate → PR raised → cost check.

request.description: E2E Step 1: Trigger SonarQube scan. Note the `newFindings` count.

exec: console.log('E2E Step 1 complete. New findings:', json.newFindings);

request.description:
E2E Step 2: Wait ~10–30s for cb-agent to pick up the scan results, then check DETECTED vulns.

Test script saves the first vulnerability ID for subsequent steps.

exec: console.log('No DETECTED vulns yet — wait and re-run');

request.description:
E2E Step 3: Wait ~30–120s for cb-agent LangGraph4j to complete, then check vulnerability status.

Expected: status changes from IN_PROGRESS → FIX_GENERATED

exec: console.log('Fix is progressing! Current status:', v.status);
console.log('Status still:', v.status, '— LangGraph4j may still be running');

request.description:
E2E Step 4: Wait ~2–5 min for cb-patcher build+test and cb-pr OPA check.

Expected: vulnerability status reaches PR_RAISED and a GitHub PR is visible in the repository.
E2E Step 5: Verify cost tracking is working. Should show non-zero spend if GPT-4o was used (CRITICAL/BLOCKER), or $0 if Ollama handled it (MAJOR/MINOR/INFO).

exec: console.log('E2E Step 5 — Cost (24h): $', c.totalCostUsd, '| Tokens:', c.totalTokens);

request.description: E2E Step 6 (optional): Check if any vulnerabilities were escalated. Expected for CWEs with very complex fixes (confidence < 0.70 after 3 retries).
